arguments.decision: What should verify_ptg file return for a single-tile file that does not satisfy the existing sprite contract (a different profile or a damaged supported sprite)?
arguments.evidence: Independent review of the new verifiers (agent finding, reproduced or plausible) reported: (1) corpus mode never asserts the corpus is complete: a mirror with 10 .ptg files removed returned pass with files 538, unpaired .msh/.mih skipped silently; (2) end flags in the middle of a span pass and a lone flag-7 final block is accepted; (3) decode memory grows unbounded for large spans and deinterleave allocates per channel for an empty payload. Measured facts: corpus has 305 spans (largest 80,496 bytes, median 17,520); every span has exactly one end-bit block (206 spans, flag 3) or exactly two (99 spans, flag 1 then flag 7 whose 14 data bytes are all 0x77); milestone formats check already verifies all 990 files by full SHA-256 against an independent archive read; notes/extracted-manifest.tsv holds a 16-hex sha1 prefix per file; milestone issue #2 requires missing required evidence to be incomplete, unsupported items listed, bounded processing, claims limited to what is measured.
arguments.priorities: Missing or unsupported evidence must not look like success; issue #2 allows other PTG profiles to be explicitly unsupported but not silently skipped; use the existing three statuses.

candidates.description: Return status incomplete (exit 2) with a top-level diagnostic naming the sprite contract failure, so a single-file run cannot be mistaken for a pass; corpus mode still lists such files as single_unsupported without failing.
Keep pass with the diagnostic only inside details.
Return fail for any file outside the sprite contract.
Invent a new status value for unsupported.

requirements: A damaged supported sprite is not reported as pass in single-file mode.
The 24 corpus files outside the sprite profile are still listed, not failing the corpus check.
